Summary:
The paper introduces a nine-facet framework (functionality, referent, generality, location, embodiment, paradigm, actor, character, nature) plus associated “edges” to give a stable, multidimensional description of AI systems and of AI as a discipline. Using 20 years of AAAI/IJCAI proceedings and ~50 years of AI Topics material, the authors map keywords onto the facets, reveal historical trends and release the full data, code and an online visualisation platform. The core safety-relevant claim is that, without such a structured, continuously updated map, governance, funding and safety oversight are mis-directed because the field’s boundaries and internal emphases shift rapidly and opaquely.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[87]
The fabric connects every risk to interventions through all mandatory intermediate node categories and shares nodes across paths, forming a single connected structure. JSON has been dry-run validated. Instruction improvements: 1) supply an explicit list of “section titles” in the prompt to ensure uniform citation; 2) clarify whether interventions may cover governance/policy or must be technical.

Inference strategy justification:
The article is methodology-oriented, so direct safety interventions are not explicit. Moderate inference (confidence 2) is used only to turn the presented monitoring platform and governance suggestions into two concrete interventions, clearly marked.

Extraction completeness:
14 nodes (~1 per 365 words) include every distinct risk→intervention reasoning step discussed (unclear contours, paradigm neglect, nine-facet insight, quantitative implementation, validation trends, governance tools, funding realignment). All edges routed through the six concept categories; no isolated nodes remain.

Key limitations:
• Paper provides no quantitative efficacy of proposed governance actions; edge confidences are thus ≤3.  
• Interventions are policy–level rather than algorithmic; findings may need separate effectiveness studies for technical safety contexts.
